transcript.text: people say AI can predict no-shows. is that real or hype?
transcript.text_fa: می‌گن هوش مصنوعی می‌تونه نیومدن بیمارها رو پیش‌بینی کنه. واقعیه یا فقط هیاهوئه؟

transcript.text:
It's real, but it has limits. If you have a record of past bookings and which ones were no-shows, a model can usually tell higher-risk bookings from lower-risk ones. That's often useful. It gives you a likelihood for each booking, not a certainty about any one person. How much it helps depends on what you can do with the warning, such as sending reminders, overbooking a little, or calling the risky bookings. To tell you whether it's worth it for you, I need to know your situation. What kind of no-shows are you dealing with, and what would you do differently if you knew in advance which ones were likely?

What kind of no-shows are you dealing with (appointments, reservations, classes, something else), and what would you do differently if you knew in advance which ones were likely?
transcript.text_fa:
واقعی است، ولی محدودیت‌هایی دارد. اگر سابقه‌ای از نوبت‌های قبلی و اینکه کدام‌ها نیامدند داشته باشید، یک مدل معمولاً می‌تواند نوبت‌های پرریسک‌تر را از کم‌ریسک‌تر تشخیص بدهد. این اغلب مفید است. برای هر نوبت یک احتمال به شما می‌دهد، نه قطعیت درباره‌ی هیچ فرد خاصی. اینکه چقدر کمک می‌کند بستگی دارد به اینکه با این هشدار چه کاری می‌توانید بکنید، مثل فرستادن یادآوری، کمی بیشتر از ظرفیت نوبت دادن، یا تماس گرفتن با نوبت‌های پرریسک. برای اینکه بگویم برای شما ارزشش را دارد یا نه، باید وضعیت‌تان را بدانم. با چه نوع نیامدنی سروکار دارید، و اگر از قبل می‌دانستید کدام‌ها احتمالاً نمی‌آیند، چه کاری را متفاوت انجام می‌دادید؟

transcript.text:
That's a good start. Two years of bookings from three dentists is plenty to work with. You don't need to know what's in the system yet. Once you pull an export, we can look at it together. When you do, ask for one row per appointment, with as much of this as the software gives you:
- the appointment date
- the dentist
- the date it was booked
- whether the patient is new or returning
- whether they attended, cancelled or didn't show

You don't need names or phone numbers. The most important column is the attended/missed one, because without it nothing can be learned from the history. If it's there, I can tell you quickly what the data can and can't do. I'm assuming you or your reception team would be the ones acting on this, with the day-before calls or filling slots. Who would that be in practice?

به اسم‌ها یا شماره‌تلفن‌ها نیازی ندارید. مهم‌ترین ستون، ستونِ آمده/نیامده است، چون بدون آن از سابقه هیچ چیزی نمی‌شود یاد گرفت. اگر آن باشد، می‌توانم سریع بگویم داده چه کاری می‌تواند بکند و چه کاری نمی‌تواند. فرض می‌کنم شما یا تیم پذیرش‌تان کسانی هستید که بر اساس این اقدام می‌کنید، با تماس‌های روز قبل یا پر کردن وقت‌های خالی. در عمل چه کسی خواهد بود؟

transcript.text: Sending more texts is a reasonable thing to try, and it doesn't rule out the rest. It's cheap, so you could start it now. Your history would then tell you whether texts are enough or whether a few high-risk bookings are causing most of the misses. Your front desk already makes calls, so a ranked call list could fit into what they do now. Here are three ways to go. Which one fits where you are?

choices.title: Look at your history first
choices.what: Once you have an export, DCLab counts how many appointments were missed and where it clusters: by dentist, day of the week, how far ahead it was booked, and new versus returning patients. You get: Plain numbers on what no-shows cost you and who they come from. That tells you whether more texts, targeted calls or a model is worth it. Trade-off: It describes the past and doesn't score tomorrow's bookings. It needs an attended/missed column in the export. Effort: Small. A short job once the export is shared.

choices.title: A model that ranks upcoming bookings by no-show risk
choices.what: DCLab builds a model from your two years of history. It would give the front desk a ranked list of the next day's appointments, so they know who to call first or which slots to try to fill. You get: A risk score for each booking, tested on appointments the model hasn't seen so you can see how well it works. Trade-off: It needs a reliable attended/missed column and some detail per booking, like booking date or new versus returning. It gives likelihoods, not certainties. If your no-shows look random, it may not beat simply texting everyone. Effort: Medium. It needs the export first, then a build you approve.

choices.title: Talk through texts versus calls, no data needed
choices.what: I explain how reminder texts, confirmation replies and targeted calls usually compare for a small clinic, and what a sensible first step would be. You get: Guidance you can act on this week, without waiting for the software people. Trade-off: It's general guidance, not based on your numbers, so it can't say what would work at your clinic. Effort: Very small. A conversation.

transcript.text:

- how often appointments are missed overall

- how far ahead the missed bookings were made

If a few kinds of booking cause most of the misses, a targeted call list makes sense. If the misses are spread evenly, more texts are probably the better first move. Nothing can run until the table exists. If you or the software people can get it, ask for one row per appointment with the date, the dentist, the date it was booked, new or returning, and attended/cancelled/no-show. transcript.text:
Asking the front desk first makes sense. They use the software every day, so they may already know where the reports are. Here is a short note you can pass on:

*"Can you run a report of all appointments from the last two years and save it as a spreadsheet (Excel or CSV)? One row per appointment. I need the appointment date, the dentist, the date it was booked, whether the patient is new or returning, and whether they attended, cancelled or didn't show. Please leave out names and phone numbers. If some of those fields aren't in the report, send what you can get."*

- **If the report has the attended/missed column**, share the file here. DCLab will count how often appointments are missed and where the misses cluster. That will show whether a call list or more texts is the better first move. - **If it has no attended/missed column**, the history can't show us anything yet. Ask the front desk whether the software marks a "no-show" or "failed to attend" status somewhere else. If it doesn't, the software company would be the next call. - **If you only get a few of the other fields**, that's fine. We'll work with what's there and say plainly what it can't tell us. Once the file is here, I'll read it and tell you what it can and can't answer before we go further.
transcript.text_fa:
اول پرسیدن از پذیرش منطقی است. آن‌ها هر روز از نرم‌افزار استفاده می‌کنند، پس شاید همین الان بدانند گزارش‌ها کجا هستند. این یک یادداشت کوتاه است که می‌توانید به آن‌ها بدهید:

*«می‌توانید یک گزارش از همه‌ی نوبت‌های دو سال گذشته بگیرید و آن را به‌صورت صفحه‌گسترده (Excel یا CSV) ذخیره کنید؟ برای هر نوبت یک ردیف. تاریخ نوبت، دندانپزشک، تاریخی که نوبت گرفته شده، اینکه بیمار جدید است یا قدیمی، و اینکه آمده، لغو کرده یا نیامده را لازم دارم. لطفاً اسم‌ها و شماره‌تلفن‌ها را نگذارید. اگر بعضی از این فیلدها در گزارش نیست، هر چه می‌توانید بگیرید بفرستید.»*

- **اگر گزارش ستون آمده/نیامده را دارد**، فایل را اینجا به اشتراک بگذارید. DCLab می‌شمارد که نوبت‌ها چند وقت یک بار از دست می‌روند و نیامدن‌ها کجا جمع شده‌اند. این نشان می‌دهد که لیست تماس یا پیامک بیشتر قدم اول بهتری است. - **اگر ستون آمده/نیامده ندارد**، سابقه هنوز نمی‌تواند چیزی به ما نشان بدهد. از پذیرش بپرسید که آیا نرم‌افزار جای دیگری وضعیت «نیامده» یا «حاضر نشده» را علامت می‌زند. اگر نمی‌زند، تماس بعدی با شرکت نرم‌افزار است. - **اگر فقط چند تا از بقیه‌ی فیلدها را بگیرید**، اشکالی ندارد. با هر چه هست کار می‌کنیم و صاف و ساده می‌گوییم چه چیزی را نمی‌تواند به ما بگوید. وقتی فایل اینجا باشد، آن را می‌خوانم و قبل از اینکه جلوتر برویم به شما می‌گویم به چه سؤال‌هایی می‌تواند جواب بدهد و به چه سؤال‌هایی نه.

transcript.text: Ok, that note is useful. I'll give it to the front desk girls today and see what they can pull. Might take them a bit, they're busy. I'll come back when I have a file.
transcript.text_fa: باشه، آن یادداشت به درد می‌خورد. امروز به دخترهای پذیرش می‌دهمش و می‌بینم چه چیزی می‌توانند بیرون بکشند. شاید کمی طول بکشد، سرشان شلوغ است. وقتی فایل را داشتم برمی‌گردم.

transcript.text: Sounds good. Take your time with the front desk, and come back when you have the file, even if it's only part of what we asked for. When it arrives, I'll first check what's in it and tell you what it can and can't answer. Then DCLab will count your missed appointments and show where they cluster. That will tell us whether a day-before call list or more texts is the better first move.
transcript.text_fa: خوب است. با پذیرش عجله نکنید، و وقتی فایل را داشتید برگردید، حتی اگر فقط بخشی از چیزی باشد که خواستیم. وقتی برسد، اول بررسی می‌کنم چه چیزی در آن هست و به شما می‌گویم به چه سؤال‌هایی می‌تواند جواب بدهد و به چه سؤال‌هایی نه. بعد DCLab نوبت‌های ازدست‌رفته‌تان را می‌شمارد و نشان می‌دهد کجا جمع شده‌اند. این به ما می‌گوید که لیست تماس روز قبل یا پیامک بیشتر قدم اول بهتری است.
